desc: Derive/verify the binomial expansion formula and the sweep invariant (T_m includes S_0..S_{r−1} before processing r); hand-check sample 1 (N=3, K=2 → 75).

Write the complete numpy solution (input parsing, cumsum prefix sums mod p, power arrays P[0..K], exclusive prefix sums T[0..K], coefficient dot-products, final mod) with careful index alignment and overflow-safe reductions.
Add a pure-Python fallback path (guarded by try/except ImportError on numpy) using the single-sweep incremental T update with precomputed coefficients.
Mentally test against samples plus edge cases (N=1 with A=0 → 0, K=1, A_i = p−1, 0⁰ = 1 convention for m=0); output is a single non-negative integer < 998244353.
Sanity-check worst-case performance (N=2×10⁵, K=10): ~30 vectorized numpy passes, no Python-level loop over N; int64 overflow bounds verified (cumsum ≤ 2⁴⁸, products reduced before summing).
